explanation: Treat each row as the bottom of a histogram of consecutive true cells. A monotonic stack finds the largest histogram rectangle, and the best over all rows is the largest all-true submatrix.
timeComplexity: O(rows × columns) Each cell updates one height and each histogram index is pushed/popped at most once per row.
spaceComplexity: O(columns) The height array and monotone stack each contain at most c columns.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: For each row, a histogram height equals the number of consecutive true cells ending there. Every all-true rectangle has some bottom row and is exactly a histogram rectangle on that row. The stack evaluates the largest such histogram rectangle, so maximizing over bottom rows is complete.
walkthrough: For [[true,true,false],[true,true,true]], the second-row histogram is [2,2,1]. Its first two columns support height 2 and width 2, giving area 4, larger than the full row’s area 3.
edgeCases: A false cell resets its column height.
A wide short rectangle may beat every square.
An empty matrix has area zero.
